text.p: Brokerage IMI Sigeco cut its earning forecasts for Renault for 1996 and the two following years and reiterated its sell recommendation on shares in the carmaker after its weak first-half results issued this week.

"Renault gave a profit warning for the second half of 1996. First, the loss in the automotive division is set to widen and show only a marginal improvement from the 1.3 billion franc record loss in the second half of 1995. The reasons are the expected collapse in French car sales in the fourth quarter after the expiry of the Juppe incentive at the end of September and the new model introductions," it said in a research note.
"Second, the truck division is expected to report an operating loss," analyst Sabine Blumel wrote. "We have therefore cut our earnings estimates for 1996-1998."

IMI cut its 1996 estimate to a loss of 2.8 francs per share instead of a profit of 2.6 francs. For 1997 and 1998 it lowered its EPS estimates to 0.4 franc and 5.0 francs, respectively, from 5.0 francs and 8.2 francs.
"We are of the opinion that, only after the introduction of the next Clio at the end of 1997, will the (car) division be in the position to report a marked improvement," the note said.
